Question: Using task1_data_and_tasks/data/mendota.csv, what was the mean water temperature (deg C) at Lake Mendota during July 2026? Reply with one number to 2 decimals.
Result: Solved (2 attempts)
Feedback received on incorrect attempts:

Code executed:

import pandas as pd
p='task1_data_and_tasks/data/mendota.csv'; d=pd.read_csv(p,comment='#'); d['timestamp']=pd.to_datetime(d.timestamp); x=d.loc[d.timestamp.dt.month.eq(7)&d.water_temp_qc.eq(0),'water_temp_C']; x=x[x>-100]; print(len(x),x.mean(),f'{x.mean():.2f}')
```
Final output answer: 22.06

--- Episode [T3] ---
Question: Using task1_data_and_tasks/data/mendota.csv, how many hourly readings exceeded 25 deg C at Lake Mendota on July 10, 2026? Reply with one integer.
Result: Solved (1 attempt)
Code executed:
```python
import pandas as pd
p='task1_data_and_tasks/data/mendota.csv'
d=pd.read_csv(p,comment='#'); d['timestamp']=pd.to_datetime(d.timestamp)
x=d.loc[(d.timestamp>=pd.Timestamp('2026-07-10 08:00'))&(d.timestamp<pd.Timestamp('2026-07-11 08:00'))&d.water_temp_qc.eq(0),'water_temp_C']
print(int((x[x>-100]>25).sum()))
```
Final output answer: 1.0
